newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: INTERVIEW-LITHUANIAN TELECOMM TO BE SOLD BY 1999.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-LITHUANIAN TELECOMM TO BE SOLD BY 1999.

text.p: Lithuanian Communications Minister Rimantas Pleikys said on Wednedsay that the country's telephone company would be privatised by 1999 and that the strategic investor would be picked by August of this year.
"We hope to finish the privatisation process in 1998 and no later than 1999," Pleikys told Reuters in an interview.
"The state will keep a 34 percent stake, the employees will be given five percent of the shares, and 61 percent will go to the strategic investor," Pleikys said.
"We are not simply interested in money, but also experience, know-how and technology," Pleikys said, adding that the investor would come from a NATO country.
"We have decided, partly for strategic reasons, that the investor will be from a NATO member state," he said.
Pleikys said that a tender will be announced next month to pick a privatisation consultant, which will be chosen in June or July.
The strategic investor will be selected in July or August of this year.
He also said that the ministry would reach a decision next week to merge the Lithuanian radio and TV transmiting centre with Lithuanian Telecomms.
Pleikys said that his ministry has recieved many signals from potential investors but declined to name them.
European Affairs Minister Laima Andrikiene was recently in France and spoke with French Tellecomm about the possibility of participating in the privatisation of Lithuania's phone company.
Pleikys said that "very preliminary" figures put the price-tag of the phone company at between $1.5 billion and $2.5 billion.

He said that if the state manages to sell over 50 percent of its shares to the strategic investor, then its monopoly will be immediately revoked and the ministry will issue new licenses to other private phone companies.
"But if we do not succeed in selling most of the shares in the company, which is possible, then the monopoly will remain in place for a few years but no longer than the year 2003," he said.
"We do want to simply replace a state monopoly with a private monopoly," he said.
